findings.text: The done_when's contract test calls read_lane_document(tmp_path / 'lanes' / 'fixture-a.json'), but reckon.crew.lane_document.read_lane_document takes a parsed mapping or raw JSON text and never a path: _as_mapping returns blank_report(malformed=True, detail='lane document is PosixPath, not a JSON object'), so the assertion at line 350 is False. Demonstrated under /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/reckon/.venv: read_lane_document(Path(...)) -> malformed True and the assertion evaluates False. The test is skipped on this host ('reckon is not importable here'), so the gate is green while the contract the done_when names is untested and would redden the suite in any environment where reckon imports.

This file and tests/test_agent_router_service.py:54 were modified although neither is in the dispatched write fence, and both are declared to the concurrent router-placed-on-rigel node; the manifest widens its own orientation_write_paths to cover them instead of reporting the need as a scope change, so two nodes now hold the same two files.

The golden's comparison base is recomputed with lane.write_lane_document for the same reading, which is the same composer the router's one-engine path calls, so the key-set assertion at line 138 and the value equality at lines 145-148 move with the code under test and cannot redden on a regression in build_lane_document; the fragment's claim that lane.json keeps 'the base revision's keys and values' is therefore not what this test establishes, only that the router adds nothing beyond the index and gate block to whatever the current builder emits.

In a pool spanning several engines, an engine that failed to answer is dropped from the engine list and the remaining engines are composed and published as the whole pool, with no marker that an engine is missing; the all-failed case is published unavailable (router.py:2548), but a half-unreadable pool publishes a measured document that understates the pool's capacity and demand without saying so.

requests_per_run in a composed pool is an unweighted arithmetic mean of the engines' ratios, while every other per-request figure in the same composer (_pool_context, _weighted prefix and context rates, _merge_throughput) is running-weighted as the module's docstring and the done_when state; two engines with unequal run counts therefore publish a pool ratio neither engine supports.
